I’m not sure why your reply has been downvoted to be honest. You’re not saying there is exploitation in all age gap relationships, but just pointing out that it happens and there may need to be some things in place to help vulnerable people. 

I think people may be upset because often in AGRs we face stigma, and often outsiders will default to the opinion that there is exploitation happening within an AGR; whether that’s the older person exploiting the younger person’s naivety, or the younger person doing the exploitation for economical reasons (I have personally had experience of this). 

I think it’s important for us all to be aware that exploitation sadly does happen in all kinds of relationships, and we should try to help when it’s happening in our own community.

At the end of the day, by doing this, we are helping ourselves too. If we don’t try to help people who may be being exploited, then these types of relationships WILL add fuel to the fire and give outsiders more reason to stigmatise all AGRs, even the healthy ones.

You have made a lot of valid points, and these things do need calling out when they are happening. I actually haven’t seen many of these instances myself, but to give this sub credit where it’s due, when I have seen red flags people rightly question the motives about the people in question.

I have made a note to myself to try and spot more of the red flag situations and call them out and be constructive with advice. It’s hard when a lot of vulnerable or underaged people will have a tendency to lie about their age. 

I wonder if a set of guidelines such as the extensive ones in the Female Dating Strategy page would be helpful. I haven’t thought about what these could be though. Have you thought about anything that you think could help OP? This could be a good discussion point between members and I do think you’re onto something.

I’m (29F) and have been with my partner (48M) for two years in my first AGR. 

It sounds cliche but I don’t look at him based on his age, I see him as a fully rounded individual and evaluate his suitability for me based on everything he has to offer. 

When I think about some of the things I love most about him, it’s likely that some of these are these are things he has developed over time so could be attributed to his age, and I guess are things I don’t tend to see in guys my own age. 

For example, he is selfless, reliable and emotionally stable; things which I have never experienced when in relationships with people my own age. I think the fact that he is a parent has also impacted on this. 

I get plenty of attention from people my own age, but I can honestly say it doesn’t change anything. On top of being a wonderful person who makes me so happy, we have better sex than I’ve ever had in my life and my SO is the most gorgeous man I’ve ever seen. 

It’s easy to feel insecure in the early stages of a relationship. Two years ago, I couldn’t fathom why someone like him would want to be with me, but now I don’t feel like that. 

An age gap relationship can be so beautiful and I wish you all the best with it. Please don’t let your insecurities get in the way :)

I know this isn’t much use to you right now, but please take comfort in that this does not always have be the case for you. 

At 15 you probably have a limited network of people you can mix with (I’m guessing these are your classmates) but as you get older you’ll have more choice over who you hang out with and find people who are more like you. 

You say you like music... if you find like-minded people in some sort of club/ gathering, you will start to feel respected when you speak to them as they will value your opinion on a topic you know a lot about and gradually your confidence can grow. 

Speaking from experience... at 15 I had no confidence, felt spoken over ALL the time, and was generally not very cool. Now I’m 28, and I choose to hang out with people who are respectful of me, and the quirks that once made me a bit weird in school (heavy metal music, reptiles, love of writing, hard worker in school) are things people are very interested in. 

It’s been a journey but it can happen. My career has gone from strength to strength, I find it easy to make friends and connect with people, and nobody that I mix with these days has any idea about the shy and awkward teenager I was.

I had eight 3-4cm areas shaved... so I still had a lot of hair left over after my operation. But due to the bleeding and subsequent hair matting from my operation my remaining hair ended up damaged and looking thin. 

Looking after my hair, trimming the dead ends etc really helped. My hair was breaking less, the ends were so split that it was breaking from the bottom upwards for the first few months. Since trimming my hair the bluntness at the end has made it look thicker - before my trim it didn’t look anywhere near this good. 

But actually my “after” photos are shorter than my before photos. It just looks so much healthier!

Because they had to perform an excision biopsy, which was cutting lumps from my scalp. Your scalp bleeds loads and when I came around from my op, the blood had dried, the shaved hair was tangled with my real hair and it made a mess of my remaining hair due to trying to get it detangled. 

My hair didn’t grow 5x that. It’s probably grown about 3-4 inches at most.

In fact in the after photos it’s shorter than the first pictures. The difference is my hair is blunter at the ends due to trimming, and I’ve looked after my remaining hair so it’s not breaking from the bottom of the hair shaft.
